title: Ledger Limitation and Recommended Task ORM Mapping
objective: Map Limitation and RecommendedTask to the shared API SQLAlchemy Base with stable identities, restrictive Run ownership, domain-derived checks, and static PostgreSQL verification without database operations.
scope: Exactly two API-Base annotation ORM records in the explicit quantmind2 schema.
Stable global primary IDs, explicit A1b2 Run/object uniqueness, restrictive Run foreign keys, domain-derived enum checks, content checks, and query indexes.
Dialect-only PostgreSQL DDL compilation, targeted tests, annotation ORM contract, Project Memory updates, and one independent local commit.
explicit_non_goals: No Component Catalog or future Task foreign key, relationship collection, status update, automatic Task creation/execution, upsert, merge, or overwrite behavior.
No Domain-to-ORM mapper, production Repository, Session, Unit of Work, transaction, database connection, credentials, migration, schema/table creation, or executed DDL.
No Manifest Parser/Indexer, Git consistency service, API, UI, TDX, Dataset Snapshot, Factor DSL, Optimization, Validation runtime, Registry, LightGBM, or Qlib change.
No Factor Lab, dependency, lockfile, runtime configuration, accepted ADR, historical Implementation Run, or A2a2c change.

known_limitations: No Domain/ORM mapper, migration, schema/table creation, live PostgreSQL, production Repository, Session, Unit of Work, transaction, Parser/Indexer, Git consistency service, API, or UI exists.
Component Catalog membership and future Task existence are intentionally not database-validated.
Static DDL compilation used SQLAlchemy 2.0.51 while production requirements pin 2.0.25.
ORM metadata alone cannot prevent privileged direct UPDATE or enforce Repository exact replay and immutable conflict.
Context and Manifest schema v1 cannot encode exact next task QM2-P0-002A2a2c in machine recommended-task arrays, so legal parents QM2-P0-002 and QM2-P0-002A2 are used there.
The containing commit cannot be embedded self-referentially; Git history resolves it after commit.
unresolved_questions: How should A2a2c represent logical repository identity while retaining globally stable annotation IDs?
How will a future Repository distinguish exact replay from immutable conflict without an unsafe upsert?
How will pinned SQLAlchemy 2.0.25 and an isolated PostgreSQL fixture be supplied?
rollback_information: Revert the single containing commit. No database, schema, migration, data, API, runtime, model, Qlib, UI, dependency, lockfile, configuration, accepted ADR, or Factor Lab rollback is required.
security_impact: ORM metadata contains no credentials and import performs no filesystem, environment, network, Git, engine, session, connection, or DDL operation; domain secret validation remains authoritative.
data_lineage_impact: No research or annotation data changed; two metadata targets prepare a future derived Ledger query index while Git Reports, Manifests, ADRs, and Implementation Runs remain authoritative.
